✓ Biotic stress.fact: Biotic stress is stress that occurs as a result of damage done to an organism by other living organisms, such as bacteria, viruses, fungi, parasites, beneficial and harmful insects, weeds, and cultivated or native plants. It is different from abiotic stress, which is the negative impact of non-living factors on the organisms such as temperature, sunlight, wind, salinity, flooding and drought.

✓ Biotin deficiency.fact: Biotin deficiency is a nutritional disorder which can become serious, even fatal, if allowed to progress untreated. Biotin deficiency rarely occurs among healthy people because the daily requirement of biotin is low, as many foods provide adequate amounts of it, intestinal bacteria synthesize small amounts of it, and the body effectively scavenges and recycles it in the kidneys during production of urine.

✓ Bipartite graph.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Bipartite graph.question: The _____ was Graph divided into two independent sets.
✓ Bipartite graph.fact: In the mathematical field of graph theory, a bipartite graph (or bigraph) is a graph whose vertices can be divided into two disjoint and independent sets U {\displaystyle U} and V {\displaystyle V} , that is, every edge connects a vertex in U {\displaystyle U} to one in V {\displaystyle V}. Equivalently, a bipartite graph is a graph that does not contain any odd-length cycles.

✓ Bipartite graph.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Bipartite graph.question: Factor graphs and _____ graphs are examples of this
✓ Bipartite graph.fact: Factor graphs and Tanner graphs are examples of this. A Tanner graph is a bipartite graph in which the vertices on one side of the bipartition represent digits of a codeword, and the vertices on the other side represent combinations of digits that are expected to sum to zero in a codeword without errors.

✓ Bipartite graph.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Bipartite graph.question: A factor graph is a closely related belief network used for probabilistic decoding of _____ and turbo codes
✓ Bipartite graph.fact: A factor graph is a closely related belief network used for probabilistic decoding of LDPC and turbo codes.

✓ Bipartite graph.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Bipartite graph.question: In computer science, a _____ net is a mathematical modeling tool used in analysis and simulations of concurrent systems
✓ Bipartite graph.fact: In computer science, a Petri net is a mathematical modeling tool used in analysis and simulations of concurrent systems. Petri nets utilize the properties of bipartite directed graphs and other properties to allow mathematical proofs of the behavior of systems while also allowing easy implementation of simulations of the system.

✓ Bipolar encoding.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Bipolar encoding.question: The _____ was Type of line code where two nonzero values are used.
✓ Bipolar encoding.fact: In telecommunication, bipolar encoding is a type of return-to-zero (RZ) line code, where two nonzero values are used, so that the three values are +, −, and zero. Standard bipolar encodings are designed to be DC-balanced, spending equal amounts of time in the + and − states.

✓ Bipolar encoding.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Bipolar encoding.question: B8ZS is a newer format for _____, where HDB3 is the original line coding type used in Europe and Japan
✓ Bipolar encoding.fact: B8ZS is a newer format for North America, where HDB3 is the original line coding type used in Europe and Japan.

✓ Bipolar encoding.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Bipolar encoding.question: Because of the way _____ was coupled to the NICAM like digital audio subsystems for the MAC family, up to 50% of data reduction was possible in both Stereo and Mono transmission modes
✓ Bipolar encoding.fact: Because of the way Duobinary was coupled to the NICAM like digital audio subsystems for the MAC family, up to 50% of data reduction was possible in both Stereo and Mono transmission modes. At least with some data transmission systems, duobinary can perform lossless data reduction though this has seldom been utilized in practice.

✓ Bipolar violation.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Bipolar violation.question: Alternate Mark Inversion (AMI), where ONE is represented by a pulse, and a _____ is represented by no pulse
✓ Bipolar violation.fact: Alternate Mark Inversion (AMI), where ONE is represented by a pulse, and a ZERO is represented by no pulse. Reliable transmission of data using this scheme requires a regular stream of pulses; too many zero bits in succession can cause a loss of synchronization between transmitter and receiver.

✓ Biquadratic field.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Biquadratic field.question: The _____ was Object from algebraic number theory.
✓ Biquadratic field.fact: In mathematics, a biquadratic field is a number field K {\displaystyle K} of a particular kind, which is a Galois extension of degree 4 of the rational number field Q {\displaystyle \mathbb {Q} } with Galois group isomorphic to the Klein four-group. Biquadratic fields are the simplest examples of abelian extensions of Q {\displaystyle \mathbb {Q} } that are not cyclic extensions.

✓ Birational geometry.fact: In mathematics, birational geometry is a field of algebraic geometry in which the goal is to determine when two algebraic varieties are isomorphic outside lower-dimensional subsets.

✓ Black hole.fact: === Primordial black holes and the Big Bang === In the early universe, fluctuations of spacetime may have formed areas that were denser than their surroundings.  Rapid early expansion of the universe may have allowed these areas to collapse, forming primordial black holes.  Various models predict the creation of primordial black holes ranging from a Planck mass (~2. 2×10−8 kg) to hundreds of thousands of solar masses.  Primordial black holes with masses less than 1012 kg would have evaporated by now due to Hawking radiation.  Despite the early universe being extremely dense, it did not re-collapse into a black hole during the Big Bang, since the universe was expanding rapidly and did not have the gravitational differential necessary for black hole formation.  Models for the gravitational collapse of objects of relatively constant size, such as stars, do not necessarily apply in the same way to rapidly expanding space such as the Big Bang
